transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm a graphic designer, and I can’t stop getting stuck on these awful "what if I missed something" thoughts about my design files. They are completely taking over my workday, and I just don't know what to do anymore.
Can you tell me more about these 'what if I missed something' thoughts - are they limited to your design work or do they also occur in other areas of your life?

The thoughts themselves are really focused on my design work, like worrying about a tiny typo in a footer or a wrong color code ruining a print run. But while the worries are about my projects, they spill over and ruin my personal life, cutting into my sleep and keeping me from gardening or seeing friends because I'm so stuck in my head.
Do you find yourself performing any repetitive behaviors or rituals, like repeatedly checking your design files, in an attempt to alleviate these 'what if I missed something' thoughts?

Yes, absolutely. To calm that panic, I constantly reopen the same files over and over, zooming in on every line of text, counting my checks, and re-exporting the artwork repeatedly. It eats up entire evenings, but even after all of that, I still can't convince myself it's safe to send to the client.

Do you experience significant anxiety or fear in situations where you're not working on your design files, such as social gatherings or when you're alone with your thoughts, or is your anxiety primarily triggered by the specific thoughts of making mistakes in your work?

The anxiety is almost entirely triggered by the fear of making mistakes in my design work. I don't avoid social situations or gardening because I'm afraid of them, but rather because I am so exhausted and mentally trapped by the endless cycle of checking my files. I just run out of time and energy for anything else.

Do you experience these 'what if I missed something' thoughts as intrusive, meaning they pop into your head uninvited and are difficult to dismiss, even when you're trying to focus on other aspects of your design work or personal life?

Yes, they are incredibly intrusive and pop into my head completely uninvited. They just loop constantly, hammering my brain until it feels impossible to shut off the feeling that I've ruined everything. Even when I try to focus on other things or just relax, I simply can't dismiss them.
Can you describe how you feel and what you experience when you're unable to perform these repetitive checking behaviors, such as if you're in a meeting or away from your computer?

If I'm away from my computer and can't check, the anxiety and panic build up intensely until it's completely overwhelming. My mind gets totally hijacked by those looping "what if" thoughts about a typo or a ruined print run, and I'm consumed by the dread that I've ruined a client's business. It makes it absolutely impossible to focus on anything else.
Do you feel like you have control over these 'what if I missed something' thoughts, or do they feel like they're controlling you, making it hard for you to think about anything else?

They definitely feel like they're controlling me; I have absolutely no control over them. Even when I know I've checked a file multiple times, I can't shut off the looping 'what-if' feelings. It leaves me completely stuck in my head and unable to focus on anything else.
Can you estimate how much time you spend on these repetitive checking behaviors each day, and do you feel like they are effective in reducing your anxiety about making mistakes, even if temporarily?

I spend hours on these checks every single day, to the point where entire evenings disappear and my workday is completely derailed. While rechecking does calm my panic at first, the relief is incredibly fleeting because I quickly become unconvinced that the file is actually safe. That doubt just pulls me right back into the cycle of rechecking all over again.
